incident: A protected merge reached exact Netlify production, but its push-triggered Production Release Readback was cancelled during rapid main movement. GitHub does not allow that cancelled run to be retried, so terminal closure remained open despite machine-verifiable production truth.
root_cause: The newer canonical Obligation Terminal Closure required a successful exact-SHA workflow run and did not inherit the descendant-safe production proof already used by the older Powerhouse terminalizer/writer reconciliation.
prevention_rule: Canonical terminal closure first consumes successful Production Release Readback. Only when that run is missing/cancelled may it prove current live production directly; the live release must expose BRAIN-DELIVERY-v2/BG169, a deploy id, healthy runtime/readiness, and an observed production SHA that contains the merge. A real failed readback never falls back.
